business_question: What evidence can you find whether or not the
principle applied during that time period on the Titanic?
business_answer_shown: The survival outcomes provide descriptive evidence consistent with a

pattern: adult women had a 76.8% survival rate and children had a 57.4% survival rate, compared with 17.7% for adult men. The differences are substantial, although the data alone do not establish why individual passengers were prioritized.

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: The baseline title identifies the topic but does not state the principal evidence-based takeaway.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: Business managers must interpret the bars before understanding the answer to the supplied question. The governing framework emphasizes that the title should convey the point being made.
baseline_chart_assessment.related_principle: Story / Method - Visual Story and Tell the Story with the Title

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: The most decision-relevant comparison—women and children versus adult men—is not explicitly highlighted.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: The viewer can calculate the differences visually, but the chart makes the audience perform unnecessary interpretation work instead of directing attention to the evidence most relevant to the business question.
baseline_chart_assessment.related_principle: Perception - Use the Eye-Brain System of Seeing

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: The vertical bars require more eye movement between category labels, bar heights, and values than necessary.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: A horizontal comparison provides more room for direct labels and allows the three rates and their sample sizes to be read together more efficiently.
baseline_chart_assessment.related_principle: Charts / Signs - Right Chart and Visualization as a Communication System

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: The baseline includes prominent gridlines and a large amount of unused plotting area.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: These elements do not add substantive evidence and slightly reduce the signal-to-noise ratio.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Adult women survival rate and denominator
data_fidelity_checks.notes: Source data verification produced 255 survivors among 332 adult women with known age, equal to 76.8%.
Using the supplied definition of children as passengers under age 16 and excluding missing ages produced 66 survivors among 115 children, equal to 57.4%.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Adult men survival rate and denominator
data_fidelity_checks.notes: Source data verification produced 106 survivors among 599 adult men with known age, equal to 17.7%.
The improved chart preserves the baseline definition of children as passengers under age 16 and excludes passengers whose age is missing.

The source confirms the ordering adult women (76.8%) > children (57.4%) > adult men (17.7%). Adult women exceeded adult men by 59.1 percentage points and children exceeded adult men by 39.7 percentage points.

principles_applied.change_made: Replaced the topic-style title with the takeaway title
and added a concise subtitle connecting the pattern to the supplied question.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: The audience can understand the principal evidence before examining individual values.

principles_applied.principle: Purpose - Answer a Well-Framed Analytical Question
principles_applied.change_made: Kept the three comparison groups directly tied to evaluating whether women and children experienced higher survival than adult men.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: The visualization remains focused on the supplied business question rather than introducing unrelated Titanic characteristics.

principles_applied.principle: Perception - Use the Eye-Brain System of Seeing
principles_applied.change_made: Added direct percentage-point comparisons between adult men and the two higher-survival groups.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: The magnitude of the evidence is visible immediately rather than requiring the audience to calculate differences mentally.

principles_applied.change_made: Reduced visual clutter, removed unnecessary chart borders, subdued gridlines, and retained only elements needed to interpret the comparison.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: The survival-rate differences receive greater visual attention and the signal-to-noise ratio improves.

principles_applied.principle: Charts - Select the Chart Type Effectively
principles_applied.change_made: Changed the vertical bars to horizontal bars while preserving the same quantitative comparison and zero-based percentage scale.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: Direct labels and sample sizes fit naturally beside each bar, improving scanability without changing the evidence.

improved_chart.title: Women and children survived far more often than adult men
improved_chart.accessibility_notes: The chart uses direct category and numeric labels, does not require a separate legend, retains a zero-based percentage scale, and communicates the key comparison through position, text, and annotations rather than relying on color alone. baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: Values shown are 76.8% for adult women, 57.4% for children, and 17.7% for adult men.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: The same source-verified rates and denominators are preserved: 76.8% (n=332), 57.4% (n=115), and 17.7% (n=599).

remaining_limitations: The chart shows descriptive survival outcomes; it does not by itself prove that a formal evacuation rule caused the differences.
Passengers with missing age are excluded because the child/adult classification cannot be established from the supplied age field.
The aggregate comparison does not control for passenger class, location aboard the ship, lifeboat access, or other factors that may also be associated with survival.
